runs.title: First map: open sessions, buffered clips, and local H3
runs.summary: First public research map separates the route types and preserves the main cost, hardware, and continuity limits.

runs.title: FastH3 local access, reality checked
runs.summary: FastH3 gained local Apple Silicon and DGX Spark paths, but the fastest stated local preview condition still requires about 23 wall seconds per output second.

runs.title: A broadcast can continue while FastH3 scenes hard-cut
runs.summary: Reactor’s current project documents a queue and paced RTMP broadcast, while its independently generated FastH3 clips do not retain subject, framing, or voice across boundaries.

runs.title: FastH3 autoplay is a setting, not a stream
runs.summary: Reactor’s current FastH3 contract defaults to black after a clip until a client plays the next one; an optional autoplay policy can advance ready clips but cannot supply a buffer or preserve the story.

runs.title: Four B200s do not clear FastH3’s documented 15-second deadline
runs.summary: Reactor’s current project documentation separates a roughly 15-second FastH3 build into about 15.5 seconds on four B200 GPUs and 12.9 seconds on eight; the update also records the current Director price and a local 5090 offline signal.

runs.title: A one-5090 FastH3 channel is a format claim, not a live-interaction claim
runs.summary: A new community project reports a continuous FastH3 channel on one RTX 5090, but its usable reading is condition-bound: 448×448 output, source-stated 22.1 fps, prequeued work, retimed motion, and distinct scenes.

runs.title: YoLive control-loop reality check
runs.summary: Yoroll’s provider-announced group vote route adds a public deployment shape; the cited four-second clip time is not a measured vote-to-screen result.
